meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (national level; recommended incorporation venue under this dossier: Canton of Zug for tax-optimal AG structuring and Crypto Valley Web3 ecosystem access)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified European-continental tradition; Swiss Civil Code, Swiss Code of Obligations, federal statutes, and binding jurisprudence of the Swiss Federal Supreme Court)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1986, updated by 2009 Protocol; in force 2010)
Switzerland-China Free Trade Agreement (signed 2013; in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland-United States Double Taxation Agreement on Income (signed 1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and the Republic of Korea (in force 1 September 2006), plus the broader EFTA third-country FTA network
Agreement between the European Economic Community and the Swiss Confederation (1972), establishing free trade in industrial goods

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0), Arts. 2(3), 3-4 and 8; Swiss Criminal Code (SCC, SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220), Arts. 626, 629-632 and 944-950; Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO/HRegV, SR 221.411), Art. 121 et seq.; Ordinance of the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority on Money Laundering (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.01); Federal Act on the Enforcement of International Sanctions (Embargo Act, SR 946.231); FINMA Circular 2020/1 on video and telephone identification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the biometric passport page of every shareholder, beneficial owner, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and competent apostille authority in the country of origin (passport issued by the relevant State passport office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the 1961 Hague Convention (Switzerland party since 11 January 1973); for non-Convention States, consular legalization by the Swiss Embassy/Consulate and, where required, super-legalization by the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, Register of Directors and Certificate of Incumbency for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or Registrar of Companies in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the certified extract; consular legalization route for non-Hague jurisdictions, with certified German/English/French/Italian translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill not older than three months) for each individual UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or utility provider in the country of residence, with notarized copy certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarized copy or notarized translation as required; consular route for non-Hague States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the initial share capital deposit (minimum CHF 100,000 nominal capital; CHF 50,000 paid-in minimum per Art. 632 CO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or account-holding bank of the founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer and/or apostille if demanded by the Swiss notary; original letter accepted on an inspection basis

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax clearance certificate (no-tax-arrears confirmation) for founders resident in high-risk jurisdictions or for existing corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the founder's residence or incorporation state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified German/English/French/Italian translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-deed and pre-account screening of UBOs, directors, signatories, family members and close associates against the SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) consolidated Swiss embargo and sanctions list, the UN Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list (as a banking-rail requirement for USD clearing and for Stripe/PayPal onboarding), the EU consolidated sanctions list (standard Swiss financial center practice), and a domestic Swiss criminal record extract (Strafregisterauszug) for each natural person. PEP status is defined per Art. 4 AMLA; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, including documented source of wealth and source of funds for the CHF 100,000 share capital deposit. Notaries and fiduciaries act as financial intermediaries under Art. 2(3) AMLA and must verify beneficial ownership at the 25% threshold. The POD retail activity (ISIC 4791, NAICS 454110) is classified Low_Risk_Standard by banking AML risk-tiering, but the onboarding bank retains full discretion to apply stricter documentary scrutiny.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), administered by the Federal Commercial Registry Office (EHRA) in cooperation with cantonal commercial register offices; name clearance applications are filed via the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) for the canton of the registered office (e.g., Zug). Online search and booking: www.zefix.ch.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The AG name must be formulated in a Swiss official language (German, French, Italian or Romansh according to the language of the canton of the registered office) and in Latin characters; purely foreign-language names are accepted only if directly registerable as an established exception. All UBO and director names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for commercial register filings, with the original script placed in parentheses. The legal form suffix must appear verbatim at the end of the name: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German); 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' (French); 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' (Italian). Name content must satisfy Arts. 944-950 CO: truthfulness, non-misleading character, distinctiveness from all names already registered in Switzerland, and consistency with the permitted business purpose.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Degree titles or academic designations not lawfully held
State or municipal insignia and names implying public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the Cantonal Commercial Register Office issues a written decree (Verfügung) with reasons and legal-remedy instructions. Step 1: Re-file a modified name; Step 2: File a formal written objection (Einsprache) within 30 days of notification of the refusal decree per CRO procedures; Step 3: If the objection is dismissed, appeal to the competent Cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) within the appellate period indicated in the decree (canton-specific, generally 10-30 days); Step 4: Lodge a further appeal to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court and, ultimately, to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court on grounds of violation of federal business-name law (Arts. 944-950 CO) per Art. 82 et seq. of the Federal Supreme Court Act (LTF). A precautionary name reservation may be renewed before expiry to preserve priority for an additional 180-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional. A virtual office or licensed domiciliation service is accepted for a low-risk online retail enterprise provided that the provider holds a cantonal domiciliation license, supplies a physical street address in the canton of the registered office, accepts service of process, and ensures statutory access to corporate records per Art. 958f CO. The registered seat must be a real, usable place actually maintained by the company (Art. 626 CO). A pure letterbox or PO-box-only arrangement without a contractual domiciliation provider is inadmissible; the Federal Tax Administration and cantonal tax offices may disregard a fictitious seat and re-attribute the company to the place of actual administration if no commercial substance is demonstrated.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a license-free, low-risk e-commerce entity: approximately 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced on-site verification by the Commercial Register Office, Federal Tax Administration (VAT), or cantonal tax authorities; probability rises to 20-30% where red flags are present (low payroll, no Swiss resident director, domiciliation of more than 30 entities at the same address, unexplained payment flows, or overdue filings). Social security compensation funds (AHV-Ausgleichskassen) may also conduct employer audits during the first operating period.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation of three candidate names (Zefix/Cantonal Commercial Register Office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per cantonal fee schedule; approx. CHF 50 per reserved name (budget CHF 150).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations and notarized copies of identity, address and corporate documents (English/German/French/Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translation bureau and notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 80-120 per certified page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association and incorporation public deed (incl. UBO declaration per AMLA Art. 2(3))
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary public (public deed under Art. 629 para. 2 CO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff based on share capital and time spent; approx. CHF 1,200.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for incorporation of the Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee of approx. CHF 800 plus applicable cantonal surcharge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SHAB (Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce) publication fee for the incorporation notice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office of the Official Gazette / SHAB (schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of approx. CHF 100 per insertion.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization package (five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Approx. CHF 25 per apostille under the federal tariff implementing the 1961 Hague Convention.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/KYC/AML due-diligence file prepared by a licensed fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss licensed fiduciary (professional under Art. 2(3) AMLA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 150-250 per hour; 4-6 hours including PEP, OFAC, UN and SECO screening and source-of-funds verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service (first annual fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation provider in the chosen canton (e.g., Zug)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 100-150 per month including mail handling and regulatory access.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion, board consent resolutions, and corporate secretarial file drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat-fee market benchmark of approx. CHF 1,500.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Banking introduction package, signature specimen notarization and pre-account KYC support
Contingency for fee escalation, supplementary apostilles or additional notarizations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency buffer of 8-10% of the total estimated pre-incorporation budget.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Articles 620–763 on the Aktiengesellschaft (stock corporation); registration and mandatory publication provisions under Articles 930–947; share capital and blocked funds deposit under Articles 632, 633 and 652g
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office at the place of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce / Registro di commercio); central index operated through Zefix; target scenario: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde / acte constitutif) together with the Commercial Register entry application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister / requête d'inscription au registre du commerce)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up at incorporation. The cash contribution must be deposited in a blocked escrow account opened in the future company's name with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank; the bank issues an irrevocable capital confirmation under Article 652g OR. The amount is released to the board only after the company is entered in the Commercial Register. Non-cash contributions require a statutory audit report and full disclosure in the incorporation deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the notarial deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association are hereby ratified and the subscribed share capital is confirmed as validly subscribed and paid up in accordance with Swiss law. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Association, in the Canton of Zug, Switzerland. RESOLVED, that [Director 1] is appointed President of the Board of Directors, [Director 2] is appointed a Director, and [Officer] is appointed Chief Executive Officer with sole signature authority until legally revoked. RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors instructs the notary and the Commercial Registrar to file the incorporation application, enter the Company in the Commercial Register, and arrange the required publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Registered-Office Address Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix portal (Swiss central business index) and the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed corporate name on Zefix to verify uniqueness and compliance with Article 951 OR. Confirm that the registered-office address is a real service-of-process address within the selected Swiss canton. If the target is Zug, obtain optional preliminary written confirmation from the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug that the name is registrable and the address satisfies commercial register requirements.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate name variants ending in AG/SA
Official identification documents of founding shareholders
Lease agreement or written right to use the registered-office address
Declaration of the intended business purpose corresponding to print-on-demand retail
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or challenged, submit an amended application or choose an alternative available name before notarization; if the address is deemed unsuitable, replace it with a compliant Swiss service address and update the draft Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Deed and Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary competent in the canton of the registered office (Notariat / Office du notaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of all founding shareholders, explains the statutory mandatory content of the Articles of Association under Articles 626–630 OR, and executes the public incorporation deed. The deed records the company name, registered office, purpose, share capital of CHF 100,000, classes and par values of shares, board composition, auditors if required, and the date of incorporation. All pages are certified and signed before the notary.
required_dossiers: Drafted Articles of Association (Statuten / acte constitutif)
Passports or residence permits of all founders
Declaration regarding initial paid-up capital
If non-cash contributions are made: audit report and contribution agreement
Consent of any person requiring authorisation to act as director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects or missing mandatory clauses, execute a written addendum or resign the deed before filing. The deed is not admissible for Commercial Register entry until fully cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Payment of Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or bank branch accepting formation accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked incorporation account in the name of the future company and deposit at least CHF 50,000 from a documented lawful source. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking confirmation under Article 652g OR, stating the account name, deposit date, amount, and the bank's irrevocable undertaking to dispose of the funds only after the Commercial Register entry and upon lawful instruction by the Board of Directors.
required_dossiers: Preliminary incorporation deed or notarised draft
Beneficial-owner declaration and AML/KYC forms
Proof of source of funds for the capital payment
Passports and residence permits of account signatories
Bank formation-account application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional anti-money-laundering evidence, provide sworn source-of-funds declarations and bank statements; if the bank refuses the account, select another FINMA-licensed bank and notify the notary; the capital confirmation must be reissued by the replacing bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Statutory Governance Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors named in the notarial incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first Board meeting at the registered office. Receive the bank capital confirmation, adopt the pro-forma first Board resolution, confirm the Articles and business purpose, appoint officers, allocate sole or joint signatory rights, approve the registered-office address, and decide that the blocked funds shall be released only upon effective Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Original notarial incorporation deed
Articles of Association
Bank blocked-funds confirmation under Article 652g OR
Minutes of the first organizational Board meeting
Signed specimen signatures of directors and any authorised officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a prospective director or officer cannot attend or accept, record abstention or appoint an alternative person; no Commercial Register filing is made until the Board and signatory selection is final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Commercial Register Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registro di commercio) of the canton of the registered office; online submission through the notary and eRegistry services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the official application form for entry into the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister), accompanied by the original notarial deed, certified Articles of Association, Board minutes, bank capital confirmation, director consents, specimen signatures, and declarations of no bankruptcy or disqualification. The Commercial Registrar examines legal compliance under Articles 940–943 OR; upon approval, the company acquires legal personality by entry and the entry is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Signed official Commercial Register application form
Original notarial incorporation deed
Certified copy of Articles of Association
Bank blocked-capital confirmation under Article 652g OR
Consents and specimen signatures of all registered signatories
Declaration that the company is not in insolvency or liquidation proceedings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, respond within the stated deadline, normally 10–30 calendar days, by amending the Articles or supplying supplementary declarations; if registration is refused, appeal to the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority or the competent administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal, Cantonal and Social Insurance Registration After Commercial Register Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC); the competent Cantonal Tax Office; the cantonal AHV compensation office (Ausgleichskasse); Suva or a private accident insurer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Register excerpt, use the automatic notification to tax authorities and complete the employer registration file with the AHV compensation office to obtain the employer number. Register employees with Suva or a private insurer for compulsory accident insurance under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act. If taxable annual turnover is expected to exceed CHF 250,000, apply for a Swiss VAT number through ESTV; in all cases confirm the federal, cantonal and municipal tax classification with the cantonal tax administration.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt after entry
Certified Articles of Association
Shareholder register and beneficial-ownership statement
Estimated turnover and income declaration
Employee payroll information, if any employees are engaged
VAT registration application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the automatic notification from the Commercial Register is delayed, file a direct written application with the AHV compensation office and ESTV requesting urgent assignment of employer and VAT numbers; any late fees may be reduced upon demonstration of good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal Premises, Fire-Safety and Occupational Clearance for Commercial Use
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Building Inspectorate (Baudepartement), Cantonal Fire Protection Authority (Feuerpolizei), Cantonal Labour Inspectorate, and the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the zoning and building-permit classification of the operating premises. For pure online POD retail without an in-house production facility, a commercial-office notification is sufficient; if the company operates a printing, storage, or fulfilment site, obtain an occupancy and fire-safety inspection, structural verification for equipment loads, workplace ventilation and lighting approval, and environmental registration for waste-water and waste handling.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the operating premises
Building floor plan and existing occupancy certificate
Fire-safety concept and inspection checklist
Structural load calculation or engineer's confirmation for heavy equipment
Swiss employer accident insurance certificate
Waste-disposal and water-discharge contracts, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspector issues a compliance order, submit a corrective action plan within the prescribed period; implementation deadlines may be accepted. If refusal is unjustified, appeal to the cantonal administrative authority; pending clearance, operations may be conducted through a certified third-party fulfilment partner.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) for commercial premises and occupation; Cantonal Building Inspectorate and Cantonal Fire Protection Authority for facility clearance; Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU) for environmental standards
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial/industrial operating permit (Betriebsbewilligung / permis d'exploitation) for premises used for production, storage or fulfilment; pure online POD custom-apparel retail without physical production generally requires no federal or cantonal trade licence, but any on-site printing operation is subject to building, fire-safety, labour and environmental permits from the cantonal authorities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not subject to a full environmental impact assessment for typical POD digital-printing volumes; the operation is classified as a low-impact activity and must verify exemption under Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP-Verordnung). Cantonal environmental registration is required where wastewater or VOC emission thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater containing ink or textile wash water must meet the Federal Water Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, SR 814.201) limit values for COD/BOD, suspended solids, pH, heavy metals and AOX before discharge. Air emissions must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung, LRV) VOC limits. Chemicals must be handled under the Chemicals Ordinance (ChemO/ORRChim). Textile and packaging waste must be separated and disposed in accordance with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA/TVA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance from the cantonal fire authority covering escape routes, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting and electrical hazard inspection; structural load inspection under SIA 261 for printing and storage equipment; occupational health and safety clearance from Suva or the cantonal labour inspectorate; mandatory employer accident insurance under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG/LAA); and building-fire insurance issued by the cantonal building insurer (Gebäudeversicherung) for any operated premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFD), portal: www.estv.admin.ch; for VAT registration and indirect taxes, the ESTV Central VAT Office; for direct taxes, the competent cantonal tax administration of the company's corporate seat.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not domiciled in Switzerland must appoint a fiscal representative resident in Switzerland and submit the official Swiss VAT registration application (Form 201 / 202) to the ESTV, attaching certified articles of association, commercial register extract from the home jurisdiction, proof of appointment of the Swiss representative, and an estimate of Swiss turnover. Upon approval, the ESTV issues a Swiss VAT number (UID/Tax ID). For direct tax purposes, a foreign entity with a Swiss permanent establishment or taxable presence must separately register with the cantonal tax authority of the relevant canton to obtain a cantonal tax ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not provide check-the-box classifications or hybrid entity elections for Aktiengesellschaften. Election mechanisms available under Swiss VAT law include: (i) voluntary VAT registration for persons below the CHF 100,000 turnover threshold, (ii) VAT group taxation for legally independent but financially, economically, and organizationally integrated entities, and (iii) simplified tax assessment for businesses with annual taxable turnover not exceeding CHF 5,020,000. No hybrid mismatch elections apply to foreign parent entities under domestic Swiss law; Swiss anti-hybrid rules apply in accordance with the OECD BEPS standards.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Businesses domiciled in Switzerland: annual worldwide taxable turnover exceeding CHF 100,000. Non-resident foreign entities: mandatory VAT registration where supplies performed in Switzerland exceed CHF 100,000 Swiss turnover (no threshold applies for foreign businesses supplying goods stored in Switzerland in certain cases); a Swiss fiscal representative is obligatory for all foreign VAT registrations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland currently mandates no real-time electronic invoicing, no API fiscal clearance, and no digital stamping. VAT invoices must satisfy Swiss formal requirements under Art. 26 VAT Ordinance and must use the Swiss QR-bill standard for domestic payment slips. The Federal Council has approved a roadmap introducing mandatory e-invoicing (Peppol-based) for domestic B2B transactions from January 2026; until then, exchange of invoices remains paper-based or via voluntary EDI/e-billing channels.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated where tangible merchandise is physically dispatched or transported out of Switzerland and the supplier retains reliable documentary proof of export. Supplies of services to a foreign recipient are zero-rated under Swiss place-of-supply rules if the recipient's seat or business establishment is outside Switzerland, provided the conditions of Articles 8 and 9 of the Swiss VAT Act are met. For Print-on-Demand (POD) custom apparel sales, zero-rating applies to international shipments where the goods are exported directly to the end customer and the operator maintains shipping records, electronic tracking, and customs evidence. Input VAT attributable to export sales is creditable or refundable under ordinary Swiss VAT rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrerklärung via e-dec/TARES, or Swiss SAD/export manifest)
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill evidencing dispatch to a foreign destination
Export accompanying document with Swiss customs release stamp (Ausfuhrschein)
Commercial invoice containing exporter, importer, Incoterms, goods description, and value
Packing list and sales contract or purchase order
Bank payment confirmation or SWIFT credit record evidencing settlement by the foreign buyer (secondary proof)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to enhanced documentary scrutiny by the ESTV and cantonal authorities. If the required export proof is missing or defective, the VAT initially zero-rated is retroactively assessed at the standard rate (8.1%) together with late-payment interest. Intentional or systematic supply of false export documents, fictitious POD transactions, or sham refund claims constitutes tax evasion under Article 70 of the Swiss VAT Act, leading to penalties of up to three times the evaded VAT, criminal prosecution, seizure of goods, and cancellation of the VAT registration. The federal limitation period for reassessment is ten years in cases of tax evasion; for ordinary omissions the period is five years. Export files must be retained for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — Schweizerische Nationalbank, with prudential banking and AML supervision by FINMA (Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority) and trade/export policy oversight by SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs). The SNB administers monetary policy, issues CHF, and operates the SIC clearing system; the Foreign Exchange Act (SR 941.13, in force 1 January 2023) imposes a retrospective balance-of-payments statistical reporting regime for cross-border transactions above CHF 25,000, executed via the reporting bank or directly by the reporting entity, but grants no prior-approval authority over market convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CHF is fully convertible and Switzerland maintains unrestricted current-account and capital-account liberalization, consistent with IMF Article VIII status and OECD Capital Movements Code obligations. No exchange-control license, central-bank permit, or profit-remittance authorization applies to dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, loan repayments, or capital liquidation proceeds of a Swiss AG. The Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at the statutory 35% rate applies only at distribution of dividends or Swiss bond interest and is reduced or refunded under applicable double-taxation treaties (e.g., 0% for qualifying parent-company participations under the Swiss parent-subsidiary regime; 15% for many treaty-resident private shareholders); this is a fiscal obligation, not a currency-convertibility hurdle. SNB statistical reporting obligations are ex-post, purely informational, and never a precondition to remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio of foreign currency into CHF. The POD retail company may hold 100% of USD, EUR, or GBP settlement funds indefinitely in Swiss or foreign bank accounts, and may denominate its treasury assets in any currency. Only ordinary Swiss profit taxation applies to accrued net income irrespective of currency situs: federal corporate income tax of 8.5% (effective) plus cantonal/communal flat taxes (e.g., Zug combined effective corporate income tax rate of approximately 11.85%); no tax is levied on unremitted export receivables beyond the accounting accrual basis.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: UBS Switzerland AG (successor legal entity to UBS and Credit Suisse operations)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution Blocked Account at formation; primary Operational Account (CHF/EUR/USD) post-registration
Operational Account (CHF/EUR/USD) with e-commerce settlement and SIC/SEPA connectivity
Operational Account (CHF/EUR/USD) with payment-processor interfaces for Stripe and PayPal payouts
Operational Account (CHF) with SIC instant payment and card-settlement rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for FINMA-licensed domestic Swiss fintechs; Low-Medium for offshore non-Swiss EMIs. A FINMA fintech license (Art. 1b Banking Act) permits public deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million without interest; eligible domestic providers (e.g., Radicant by ZKB, Yapeal, neon) can host low-risk e-commerce operating accounts and are fully interoperable with SIC/SEPA. Crypto-capable FINMA-licensed banks (e.g., Sygnum Bank, SEBA Bank) are viable where the Zug 'Crypto Valley' Web3 nexus triggers digital-asset settlement, though enhanced due diligence applies. Offshore EMIs (UK, Lithuania, France, Germany e-money licensed) are not members of SIX Interbank Clearing and cannot hold direct Swiss IBANs; they operate through a Swiss correspondent omnibus account in the EMI's name, exposing the merchant to sub-account segregation risk and non-bank counterparty credit risk. Legal constraints: taking deposits from Swiss resident customers requires a Swiss banking license (Art. 1 Banking Act), and a non-Swiss EMI cannot act as the primary treasury bank of the AG; it may be used only as a supplementary payout-collection rail for marketplaces, with daily zero-balancing sweeps to the principal Swiss Tier-1 account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: AMLA (SR 955.0) and the Swiss Bankers Association Due Diligence Agreement (CDB 20) require the account-holding bank to identify the contracting party, all authorized signatories, and every beneficial owner with documentary evidence. In practice, Tier-1 Swiss banks mandate an in-person KYC interview at a Swiss branch for at least one board director and for the ultimate beneficial owner, particularly when the UBO is non-resident; video identification is recognized under FINMA Circular 2021/01 for natural persons but is generally applied only to low-risk additional signatories, not to the primary foreign UBO of a newly formed AG. Remote onboarding is formally possible at digitally native banks (e.g., Radicant, neon) for a low-risk, standard-tier e-commerce structure with a clean sanctions profile and no high-risk jurisdiction nexus, but it is not recommended for the primary treasury account. Because the incorporation of a Swiss AG requires at least one director to appear physically before a Swiss notary to authenticate the articles of association (Art. 626, 698 OR), the dominant compliance practice is to bundle the notarial appointment with the bank's personal KYC interview, achieving the required Swiss physical presence in a single visit; all subsequent changes of signatories may be completed by video identification and e-banking certificate authentication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-resident UBO holding 100% of the AG with funds originating from a non-CRS or partially-CRS jurisdiction, or any nominee-shareholder structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certified copy of the deed of incorporation; current Handelsregisterauszug (Swiss Commercial Register extract) reflecting the true UBO; shareholders' register of the AG; OECD CRS and Swiss FTA registration confirmation; FATCA self-certifications of each shareholder; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation for the statutory CHF 100,000 minimum capital, including bank statements and a traceable transaction trail; formal board resolution naming signatories; and a statement of no nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency card-not-present e-commerce transactions under ISIC 4791 POD retail, with multi-currency settlement flows, chargeback exposure, and marketplace sales via Stripe and PayPal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed POD business plan and revenue model; executed print-on-demand fulfilment agreement with the apparel supplier; merchant processing agreements with Stripe and PayPal; expected monthly volumes and average order values; return/refund and dispute-handling policy; live website and order-management system evidence; track record of card-dispute ratios below Visa/Mastercard scheme thresholds; and a compliance statement confirming no prohibited goods list items.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto or Web3 nexus arising from the Zug 'Crypto Valley' strategic role, including stablecoin settlements, token-based loyalty, or crypto-capable processor integration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Mandate agreement with a FINMA-licensed crypto bank or payment provider (Sygnum, SEBA, Bitcoin Suisse); internal AML policy covering virtual-currency conversion, wallet address transparency, and fiat-off-ramp limits; definitive identification of wallet addresses and transaction monitoring logs; appointment of a Swiss AML compliance officer (Geldwäschereiverantwortlicher) registered with FINMA; and AMLA/AMLO-FINMA-compliant transaction-screening software and audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: US nexus: significant US customer base and US clearing rails (PayPal/Stripe), triggering FATCA, OFAC sanctions, and potential US permanent-establishment or VAT/GST questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATCA Form W-8BEN-E with GIIN of the Swiss AG; OECD CRS registration with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration; evidence that US customers are end-consumers creating no US-situs payor or permanent-establishment trigger; ongoing OFAC/SECO/UN sanctions screening records; transfer-pricing documentation for any US fulfilment or marketplace arrangement; and Swiss VAT registration certificate (MWST) evidencing Swiss e-commerce substance and the declaration of Swiss VAT on domestic sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Domiciliation-only registered office (letterbox indicators): no physical operating substance in Switzerland, no Swiss-resident signatory, and low transparency of operational management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed office-registration agreement (Sitzvertrag) with a licensed Swiss domiciliation provider; director service contract of a Swiss-resident individual (where applicable); office lease agreement confirming physical substance; Swiss VAT number evidencing active e-commerce operations; board minutes approving the treasury mandate and banking resolutions; and evidence of bookkeeping performed by a Swiss fiduciary or auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Statutory share capital of the CH AG is CHF 100,000 nominal, of which at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up (Art. 621, 632-633 OR). The foreign subscriber pays the capital contribution in CHF (or foreign currency converted at the SNB daily reference rate) by SWIFT MT103 directly into a blocked capital-contribution account (Kapitaleinzahlungskonto) opened in the name of the company in formation at a Swiss SIC-member bank (UBS or ZKB recommended). The bank then issues the capital-payment attestation (Kapitaleinzahlungsbestätigung) required by the notary and the Commercial Register Office; funds must be irrevocably at the free disposal of the board upon registration. For subsequent capital increases, the incoming cross-border transfer uses SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity funds) or SEPA pain.001 for EUR, referencing the company name, the ISIN/security number, and 'Kapitalerhöhung' in field 70; funds are held in a blocked sub-account until the increase is entered in the Commercial Register. No SNB or FINMA prior authorization is required; cross-border inflows above CHF 25,000 are included in the SNB balance-of-payments statistical reporting performed by the bank. The beneficiary must match the registered company name exactly and the remitter must be the subscriber to avoid an attestation delay.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For POD supplier payments (typically print-on-demand fulfilment vendors in USD, EUR, GBP, or CNY), the standard clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 open-account payment from the Swiss operational account through a correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire for USD, T2 for EUR, and CHAPS for GBP). EUR payments to EU suppliers settle via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using ISO 20022 pain.001/pacs.008 messages with near-real-time finality; domestic CHF supplier invoices settle via SIC instant payment (SIP) at 24/7/365 finality. For high-value procurement or inventory pre-financing exceeding approximately USD 250,000, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) or standby LC (ISP98) may be opened, but is uneconomic for ordinary POD open-account purchases. Marketplace and payment-processor settlements (Stripe, PayPal, Shopify Payments, Etsy) are received as daily batch payouts to the operational account; treasury policy should mandate a daily FX sweep converting surplus USD/EUR/GBP to CHF only when needed, using the bank's algorithmic FX conversion desk at mid-market rates. All disbursements require a delegated-authority matrix, dual-approval e-banking release, and positive-pay file-based reconciliation controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards (FX outrights) — permitted for hedging EUR/USD/GBP revenue streams from POD customer settlements against CHF operating expenses, under an ISDA 2002 or Swiss Master Agreement with any Tier-1 Swiss bank; maturities and notional must correspond to underlying commercial receivables.

FX swaps (swap point transactions) — permitted for treasury liquidity management, converting excess foreign-currency settlement balances into CHF for a fixed period with an agreed reverse leg, without creating open market risk.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) — permitted for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans, equity funding, or future capital expenditures, with full ISDA/CSA or Swiss Master Agreement documentation; commonly available from UBS, ZKB, and BCV dealing rooms.

European-style over-the-counter FX options — permitted for capping adverse conversion rates on non-CHF sales quotes (e.g., fixed-price USD collection sweeps) while preserving upside, subject to option-premium accounting under OR 959 and the bank's product-appropriateness assessment.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally permissible under Swiss law and not governed by exchange controls, but not market-standard and generally unavailable at Swiss Tier-1 banks for CHF because the CHF is fully convertible and always deliverable; NDFs should be considered only for illiquid emerging-market customer currencies, and only with a FINMA-regulated counterparty booking through a Swiss dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting (Generalversammlung) for approval of annual accounts, allocation of profit, discharge of the board, and re-election of the auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory minute book retained at the registered office; no filing with any regulator is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date under Art. 699 para. 4 CO; for a 31 December year-end the AGM must be held on or before 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability for unlawful refusal to convene the AGM; on shareholder complaint the court may convene the meeting; persistent organisational default allows the commercial register to impose compliance orders and ultimately seek judicial dissolution under Art. 731a CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, notes, and statutory audit report (ordinary or limited audit where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Presented to shareholders at the AGM and retained at the registered office; submitted as an attachment to the annual cantonal tax return; a listed or bond-issuing AG must additionally deposit the accounts with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office and publish in the Swiss Official Gazette
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Presentation at the AGM no later than six months after balance-sheet date, i.e., by 30 June for a calendar-year AG; publication-bound AGs must deposit and publish within the same six-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounts not approved by the AGM are without effect, the board is denied discharge, and the company may face supervisory proceedings; publication-bound AGs that default receive a commercial register warning and could be struck off after sustained non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for federal direct tax, cantonal tax, and municipal tax, including net-equity capital tax schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Steuerverwaltung) competent for the registered seat; the federal direct tax return is submitted jointly through the same cantonal authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonally fixed deadline, generally 30 to 90 days from delivery of the pre-printed return package dispatched between February and June of the year following the tax year; one written extension of up to 60 days is routinely granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessment by estimation, arrears interest of approximately 4–6% per annum, late-payment surcharge up to 5% of assessed tax, and administrative fines up to 300% of the evaded amount for intentional concealment; limitation extended to 10–15 years in evasion cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (MWST-Abrechnung) for Print-on-Demand retail turnover from the web store
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) through the Swiss electronic VAT filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each VAT period; quarterly periods are the statutory default, while annual filing is granted only by ESTV decision and remains due within 60 days after 31 December of the approved assessment period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT arrears interest currently about 3.5% per annum, a default or negligence penalty of up to CHF 8,000, and criminal sanctions with additional fines for deliberate under-declaration of taxable turnover

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss withholding tax declaration and remittance for dividends or taxable profit distributions (Verrechnungssteuer)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), Withholding Tax Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each distribution event; for regular distributions the ESTV may prescribe a semi-annual rhythm and require an annual recap on the official withholding tax form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest plus a penalty of up to 300% of the tax amount for intentional evasion; directors and the company are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted 35% withholding tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AHV/OASI employer annual salary declaration and social security contribution settlement (AHV/IV/EO/ALV and BVG where employees exist)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse/AVS) competent for the employer's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage control statement generally due by 31 January of the following year; ongoing contribution payments are settled monthly or quarterly according to the compensation office schedule and are independent of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest on unpaid contributions, administrative surcharge of up to 10% in cases of wilful default, criminal prosecution for contribution fraud, and personal liability of directors for employee contribution shares not withheld

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal structural business statistics survey (Unternehmensstrukturstatistik) — compulsory only if the AG is drawn in the annual sample
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Statistical Office (BFS/OFS), business register section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of receipt of the questionnaire; the draw rotates annually and has no fixed calendar anchor for all companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to CHF 2,000 for refusal to answer, late submission, or submission of false data pursuant to the Swiss Statistics Ordinance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit under Art. 727 CO is compulsory if the AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: CHF 20 million balance-sheet total, CHF 40 million net sales revenue, or 250 full-time employees on annual average. Below those thresholds, a limited statutory audit is the default, except that shareholders may unanimously waive the audit in writing if the AG has fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and no shareholder holding at least 10% of the voting rights requests a limited audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958–963b CO) with a single-tier balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, and notes; Swiss GAAP FER may be adopted for true-and-fair presentation; IFRS is optional for unlisted companies and mandatory only for listed groups; the audited or internally approved commercial accounts form the basis for federal and cantonal tax assessments without separate tax-basis books.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct tax on net profit after tax (Art. 68 LIFD), equivalent to ~7.8% on pre-tax profit; combined federal, cantonal, and communal aggregate statutory rate ranges from approximately 11.9% to 21.0% depending on the canton of residence (e.g., Zug ~14.8%, Zurich ~18.5%, Geneva ~21.0%).
